stages.finding: DISTINCT_DISEASE: No shared causal gene, so these are independent disease entities and any relationship between them must be argued biologically.
NOT_ASSESSABLE: No shared gene, so variant effects describe different proteins and are not comparable. Any shared mechanism must be argued at the process level instead.
no shared features on this axis
STRONG: Babinski Sign, Talipes Equinovarus, Cerebellar atrophy, Nystagmus
0 primary findings establish a direct molecular link
no direct evidence, so no bridge derived
SHARED_PHENOTYPE_ONLY (retrieval INCORRECT_AND_CONNECTION_FALSE): Overlap is confined to phenotype and anatomy, with no molecular or process-level anchor and no evidence of a direct link.

alternative_explanations.description: The diseases share symptoms without sharing a cause. Clinical overlap is common between disorders of the same organ.
The same cell type or tissue is affected by unrelated processes. A vulnerable cell population appears in many unrelated disorders.
The shared process term is broad enough to cover mechanistically distinct branches, so the annotation matches while the biology does not.
The two labels describe one disease or one allelic spectrum, so the apparent connection is nomenclature rather than biology.
The shared feature is perturbed in opposite directions, which argues against functional equivalence.
The shared gene participates in many disorders, so sharing it describes a research area rather than a specific mechanism.
One disease is far better annotated than the other, so apparent similarity or difference may reflect curation rather than biology.

final_rationale: Overlap is confined to phenotype and anatomy, with no molecular or process-level anchor and no evidence of a direct link.
